I will farm my land as a full `winter wheat -> summer maize` rotation this year. I am assuming I have `20 mu` because no land area was given; the per-mu management is the real decision. I would not switch into cotton or a mixed plan. In Quzhou, wheat and maize are the core grain crops, and the winter wheat-summer maize system is the normal local pattern. Our county is in the North China Plain, with about `518.5 mm` annual rainfall, and most rain comes in summer, so wheat needs more irrigation support and maize can lean more on summer rain. I would keep the plan simple and steady: improved winter wheat seed for a reliable stand, hybrid summer maize seed for yield, moderate fertilizer instead of chasing the highest rates, rotary tillage before wheat, and no-tillage sowing for maize right after wheat harvest so I do not lose moisture or time. I would aim for solid farm yields, not demonstration-field yields. This is based on Quzhou and North China Plain sources showing wheat-maize dominance and local work on this rotation, plus 2025 official Chinese technical ranges for wheat and maize water-fertilizer management: China Agricultural University Quzhou station, MOA wheat plan, MOA maize plan, and a Quzhou county study ([CAU Quzhou 1](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2021/12/31/art_46290_874257.html), [CAU Quzhou 2](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/2/25/art_46232_1012984.html), [MOA wheat](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202504/t20250407_6472869.htm), [MOA maize](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202504/t20250410_6473061.htm), [Quzhou study](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/13/9/2362)).
